worked_solution:
Since $-3{x}^{2}-4$ is always negative, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity, but we have to remember to flip the sign of the inequality. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3{x}^{2}-4)(x-1) & <0 \\ \frac{(-3{x}^{2}-4)(x-1)}{-3{x}^{2}-4} & >\frac{0}{-3{x}^{2}-4} \\ x-1 & >0 \\ x & >1.\end{aligned}
$$
